about: teuf-teuf historical source register: every historical or causal claim the film makes or implies, its source and status. Status: sourced | uncertain | contested | staged compression | derived (asserted in sim.py) | original. Nothing marked uncertain or contested appears on screen as fact.

claims.claim: Teuf-Teuf is a 1956 animated film by Jean Jabely, an animated history of means of transport staged on a cave-painting mural; Cité Films distributes it and supplies the reference still.
claims.note: source anchor given in prompts/teuf-teuf.md; page not re-read in this session. The film itself was not seen beyond the one still: its sequence is unknown.

claims.claim: Raymond Queneau wrote the commentary; a manuscript dossier places image descriptions beside it.
claims.note: source anchor in prompts/teuf-teuf.md. Our captions are original Queneau-like lines, not Queneau's text (R13).

claims.claim: The Ljubljana Marshes wheel (with its axle) is a Copper Age wooden wheel of the Baden culture, described as the oldest wooden wheel yet discovered.
claims.on_screen: only as the wheel cutout and the end source line ('roue des marais de Ljubljana'); no date shown
claims.note: from the Commons file title and its categories (Ljubljana Marshes Wheel, Cartwheels, Baden culture, Copper Age in Europe), read 2026-11-16.

claims.claim: The wheel is about 5,150 years old (c. 3150 BCE); its dimensions.
claims.note: the category page (Wikidata infobox) could not be read: Commons API rate-limited this session. The plan's '~5,150 years' is not verified here. Do not show a number.

claims.claim: The Ljubljana wheel was fixed to a rotating axle through a square hole (wheel and axle turn together; the axle turns in bearings under the vehicle).
claims.on_screen: implied by the cart's construction (wheel fixed to axle, axle in bearings)
claims.note: visual reading of the photograph (the axle is shown with the wheel; the hole reads as square); no text source verified this session.

claims.claim: Rollers came before wheels / the wheel evolved from the roller.
claims.note: the roller-to-wheel theory is disputed. The film shows a sequence of mechanisms under one load, not a lineage; the counter-check argues mechanically (contact kind), not historically.

claims.claim: The wall is a real rock surface at Cueva de las Manos, Río Pinturas (Santa Cruz, Argentina; Monumento Histórico Nacional ID 876) with negative hand stencils, animal figures (guanacos) and symbols.
claims.on_screen: the wall itself; end source line 'Cueva de las Manos (Suzko, CC BY-SA 3.0)'
claims.note: file description (es): 'Detalle de pinturas de manos, animales y símbolos en una de las paredes de roca'; {{Monumento Argentino|876}}; coordinates -47.148, -70.656; photo 2005-01-07.

claims.claim: The Cueva de las Manos stencils date to about 9,000-13,000 BP.
claims.note: literature range quoted in plan.md; not verified in this session.

claims.claim: Dragging, rolling on logs and the wheeled platform are shown on one wall, with the same load, the same two figures and the same 7 s push, one after the other.
claims.on_screen: declared in the end line: 'séquence mise en scène, non chronologique'
claims.note: the mechanisms belong to different places and periods; the film makes no claim that they happened here, in this order, or to one stone.

claims.claim: Scale: the boulder is 2.5 m long and the figures about 2.5 m tall at 100 px/m; the wheels are 0.72 m across; distances 1.2 / 3.0 / 8.0 m.
claims.note: the ratios between trials are the proof, not absolute sizes. The 1.2/3.0/8.0 m outcomes come from the fixture films/teuf-teuf.py and are demonstrative, not measured historical performance.

claims.claim: A load on loose rollers advances at twice the rollers' speed (rollers travel at v/2 with no slip), so rollers fall out behind and must be carried forward.
claims.on_screen: shot 3: logs drift back at v/2, log A falls out, log D carried
claims.note: rolling kinematics; asserted per frame: roll slip <= 0.5 px (max 0.012 px).

claims.claim: Dragging on a runner produces stick-slip (lurches) under a steady push.
claims.note: static/kinetic friction with the pusher's body as the spring; the numbers are chosen, not measured.

claims.claim: A wheel that is not held by an axle in bearings behaves as a roller: it drifts back under the load and drops out.
claims.note: same kinematics as R10 applied to the loose wheels.
written for this film; no line is quoted from Queneau or from Teuf-Teuf.

claims.claim: No frames, sound or text from Jabely's Teuf-Teuf are used.
claims.note: the reference still (assets/references/teuf.webp) was only measured and viewed.

claims.claim: Colossi were dragged on sledges (el-Bersheh relief of Djehutihotep, after Wilkinson); a bull colossus moved on a sledge over rollers (Kouyunjik relief, after Layard 1882).
claims.note: background only: the two engravings remain in sources/ from an earlier version but are not used by direction 1 and are not credited.
